purpose: set measurable reliability targets with users in mind and use the remaining error budget to steer work
entry_criteria: Measurement data exists or can be collected
Service owner and product owner are available
procedure: Choose SLIs that measure what users experience (availability, latency, correctness) for each critical journey.
Set SLO targets and windows from historical data and user expectations, not from aspiration alone.
Compute the error budget and define the policy: what happens when it is spent (for example pause risky releases).
Implement measurement and a dashboard; verify the SLI matches real user experience.
Review SLO attainment and budget burn on a fixed cadence.
Adjust targets with owners when evidence shows they are wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Each SLO has a clear SLI, window and target
Error-budget policy is agreed by service and product owners
SLI measurement was verified against a known event
validation_method: Service owner and product owner agree the policy.

validation.check: replay a known past outage against the SLI query and confirm it registers
validation.expect: SLI dips during the outage window
returns a ratio matching the dashboard

failure_modes.mode: SLI does not reflect user pain
failure_modes.detection: Outage did not move the SLI

failure_modes.mode: Target set above what the dependencies allow
failure_modes.response: Lower the target or fix the dependency

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A checkout journey gets an SLO of 99.9 percent success over 30 days, a budget of about 43 minutes, and a policy to freeze risky releases when 75 percent of the budget is spent.
